QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_5

question.text: Kaveri Macro Fund (close-ended Cat III, 3-year tenor) has committed capital of INR 60 crore and NAV at end of Year 3 of INR 84 crore. Hurdle rate is 10% (compounded). Manager's predetermined profit share is 20% of total profits, with a 100% catch-up clause. Hurdle Return = 60 x (1.10)^3 − 60 = INR 19.86 crore. Total profit = INR 24 crore. How much does the manager receive?

answer.text: INR 4.14 crore (entire residual after hurdle used for catch-up)
INR 4.80 crore (20% of INR 24 crore total profit)
INR 0.828 crore (20% of INR 4.14 crore residual)

explanation.text: The Logic: Manager's predetermined share = 20% x INR 24 cr = INR 4.80 cr. With 100% catch-up, residual profit after hurdle = 24 − 19.86 = INR 4.14 cr goes ENTIRELY to the manager till catch-up target (4.80 cr) is reached. Here residual (4.14 cr) is LESS than the catch-up target (4.80 cr), so the entire 4.14 cr is paid to the manager and investors receive nothing above hurdle. The Trap: INR 4.80 cr assumes enough residual exists for full catch-up — it doesn't. 0.828 cr applies 20% to residual (that's the NO-catch-up answer). 3.97 cr is 20% of hurdle return which is a nonsense split. Cross-Exam Context: Cat I/II waterfalls (XIX-D) commonly use 100% catch-up + 80/20 split. Cat III funds on XIX-E occasionally use this in close-ended structures; HWM mechanics dominate open-ended. Manager's Pro-Tip: With 100% catch-up, investors get NOTHING above hurdle until manager catches up. In a modest-return year, investors may walk away with just hurdle while manager pockets the delta. Disclose this clearly in PPM illustrations — it's a top LP complaint.
